move: knob stretches across, snaps with overshoot, sun becomes moon, world goes dark with stars
how: A large 240x130 grey toggle with a white knob holding a sun icon, a label beneath, and 40 hidden seeded stars across the stage. Toggle and label enter with back.out(2) / expo.out in the first 17% of the 3s loop. Flip on at 0.7s (23%): the knob stretches scaleX 1.35 from its left edge with power2.in, slides 110px with back.out(1.8) over 0.45s and relaxes to scaleX 1 from its right edge with elastic.out(1,0.5); the track tweens to purple and pops 1.05 with an elastic settle; the whole stage background tweens to near-black over 0.6s; the sun rotates 90 and shrinks away while a moon spins in from -90 with back.out(2); the label colour goes white and 'Light mode' rolls up to 'Dark mode'; the stars fade in with a random-order 0.01s stagger. At 2.05s (68%) the mirror sequence flips off and the stars fade, ending in the light state.
adapt: Change the two labels, the purple/dark palette, the two icons and the star count; TRAVEL = track width - knob - 20. Keep the stretch-slide-relax trio with the alternating transform origins — that is the snap.
port: mount(el, shot) builds stars (seeded with fx.rng), toggle with knob and two icons, and label pair inside el. animate returns the timeline with flips at 0.233D and 0.683D; the stage backgroundColor tween must target el (or a full-size backdrop inside el) rather than the document stage. The from() tweens need immediateRender:false.
caveats: toggle enters from opacity 0 and stays visible, so the loop restarts with an entry pop
tweens backgroundColor on the stage element, which must be scoped to the shot container
